Yemen Financial Inclusion Evidence

From rail to result: the missing middle matters

Start with a questionVerify evidence

This resource presents the strongest defensible answer while keeping scope, limits and source visible.

Evidence Readings/From rail to result: the missing middle matters
Question

When a new rail, regulation or programme exists, what evidence would show that it changed financial inclusion?

What the evidence supports

Infrastructure and reform evidence can establish rules, systems, implementation and activity. Inclusion requires additional evidence on access, use, quality and outcomes. Where the middle links are unmeasured, the evidence chain remains incomplete rather than established.

01

What supports this reading

POS infrastructure expanded: POS terminals reported by the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden) increased from 561 in March 2025 to 1,473 in January 2026.

Accounts and transactions are not unique people: Administrative accounts, e-wallet subscribers and payment transactions are not equivalent to unique people measured by Findex.

Institutional progress is not operation or outcome: During June–August 2026, official CBY-Aden records show further institution-building in the payment architecture through unified-network integration work and the establishment and governance of the Yemeni Payments and Clearing Company (YPCC); operational usage and inclusion outcomes remain separate evidence questions.

02

What qualifies or complicates the reading

The POS series is a count within the reporting scope of the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden); how far that scope covers each area of Yemen is not established, and some monthly releases show differences between displayed growth percentages and the raw totals. January 2026 was the latest monthly release on the CBY-Aden payments page as checked on 26 September 2026. The 2026 records document institutional and project steps only; they contain no measure of go-live, participation, reliability, adoption or transaction coverage.

03

How this fits into the wider system

A reform or payment rail can be real and important before its inclusion outcome is known. The transmission chain moves through distinct states: rule or programme, implementation, operation, access, use, service quality and outcome. Monitoring becomes misleading when success at one state is relabelled as success at a later state.

04

What the evidence does not establish

Regulation, infrastructure, a new institution or go-live does not by itself show access, use, quality or outcomes, and missing downstream evidence does not mean a reform failed.

05

Implication for decision use

The evidentiary state of a reform is the furthest stage actually observed. Evidence that a rail has gone live, and then of its operational coverage and reliability, is needed before its performance can be assessed; an inclusion claim requires separate evidence on access, use, quality or outcomes for the relevant population or user base.

06

What remains unknown

Evidence of go-live itself, and then comparable active-use, service-quality, complaint and population-outcome measures, are not yet available for the newest reforms and rails.

07

What evidence would change the reading

Reform-specific operational, access, use, quality and outcome indicators tied to the same implementation timeline would show where transmission succeeds, stalls or remains unmeasured.

08

Trace the reading back to evidence

Open the linked evidence records to check the definition, period, population or scope, source, derivation, limitations, evidence date and correction history behind each figure in this reading.

  • Where can people and firms actually reach financial services — and where is the map still blank?
  • Are reforms and payment infrastructure turning into access, use, quality and outcomes?

The missing middle from rail to inclusion result

Analytical text alternative
  1. Analytical question: Which link in the reform-to-outcome chain is actually evidenced?
  2. What the evidence shows: The evidence reaches the first steps of the chain only. Rules and programmes are documented: a decision of the Central Bank of Yemen – Aden (CBY-Aden) of 26 June 2024 requiring new domestic cash transfers to go through the unified transfer network, with stated exceptions; the Financial Market Infrastructure and Inclusion Project (FMIIP), which started in July 2025 with components to support a Fast Payment System in areas under the internationally recognized government, a real-time gross settlement system with an upgrade of CBY-Aden core banking, and an access-point database; and a CBY-Aden board decision of 29 March 2026 on a mandatory national QR standard, linking of e-wallets and CBY-Aden's participation as a main shareholder in the Fast Payment System operator company. Institutional steps followed in June–August 2026: unified-network integration work, the restructuring of the Unified Money Network company, and the founding assembly and first board meeting of the Yemeni Payments and Clearing Company (YPCC). The evidence also holds POS figures for January 2026 within CBY-Aden's reporting scope (1,473 terminals; 24,026 transactions) and an attributed CBY-Aden statement on unified-network activity from January 2026. Nothing here measures access by people, use, service quality or outcomes: those steps are open, which means not yet measured, not failed.
  3. Scope and time: Dates vary by reform/rail; exact event/observation dates travel with nodes · Each state retains its own administrative, provider, user or population universe
  4. What not to conclude: A rule, procurement, installation, institutional event or go-live does not by itself show access, use, quality or outcome; an open step has not yet been measured and does not mean the reform failed.
